info.title: new-workflows API
info.description: Shared business-object schemas for the sqlite-backed workflows engine rewrite (see new-workflows/plans/spec.md). No HTTP paths yet — this package exists ahead of new-workflows-http so the frontend and lib can share these types before the endpoints themselves are designed.

code.description: A short, machine-readable error code, for when HTTP status codes are not sufficient.

message.description: A human-readable description of the error.
message.example: The requested resource could not be found.

workflow-run-mode.description: Execution mode for a run, set once at `createRun` and unchanged for its lifetime. Same modes as today's `@saflib/workflows`: `dry`/`checklist` never touch the filesystem or run commands; `script` runs mechanical steps (copy, command) but skips prompts, TODO checks, and validation commands (typecheck/test); `print` hands prompts to an external agent and halts between steps; `run` drives the agent itself.

workflow-run-status.description: Lifecycle state of a run. `pending` before the first step runs; `running` after a step succeeds with more steps left; `awaiting_prompt`/ `awaiting_user` after a step hands control back to the caller (an agent prompt or a human action is needed before advancing again); `done`/ `failed` are terminal.

workflow-step-status.description: Outcome of a single step attempt row. `running` while the step is in flight (the row is inserted before the step function is called); `success`/`error` are the two terminal outcomes for a step; `awaiting_prompt`/ `awaiting_user` mean the step handed control back to the caller without finishing — the same step index will be attempted again on the next `advance` call.

workflow-log-channel.description: Which output channel a log line belongs to, so a renderer (CLI or web) can style/route it distinctly instead of guessing from content. `terminal`: raw stdout/stderr from a subprocess the workflow ran (vite, npm, git). `agent`: output from the coding agent (what it said, what it executed). `tool`: the workflow engine's own narration (e.g. "running step 3: copy"). `agent-input`: the prompt text sent to the agent.

workflow-log-level.description: Severity of a single log line, independent of its channel.

workflow-run-agent-config.description: Which agent CLI drives a run's `run`-mode steps, and its resumable session. Set at `createRun` (or when the run is retried against a different agent) and persisted on the run row so a resumed process can `--resume` the same underlying session.

cli.description: Agent CLI adapter to use. `mock-agent` is test-only (no subprocess). More CLIs (e.g. Claude Code) are expected to join this enum later.

sessionId.description: Session id returned by the agent CLI's first turn, passed back on subsequent turns (e.g. `--resume`) so multi-turn steps share context.

workflow-config-body.description:
Body of a one-off, config-defined workflow (a `workflow_config` row) — a name, an optional description, and a list of steps built entirely from the same primitives `new-workflows/lib` gives code-defined workflows, so no TypeScript is required to author one.

First-draft shape: field names and the step set will likely change once Phase 3 (config-defined workflow validation) is actually built — this is meant to make the intended structure reviewable now, not to be final.

`transform-file` is deliberately excluded: its `transform` argument is an arbitrary function and can't be expressed as data, so it stays a code-only step kind. Function-typed fields on the other step kinds (`lineReplace` on `copy`, `skipSourcePath` on `copy`) are excluded for the same reason — config-defined `copy` steps get only mechanical renames.

name.description: Human-readable name shown in the CLI/dev-site, not the run id.

description.description: Longer explanation of what this workflow does and when to use it.
description.example: Scaffolds a new feature flag: adds the flag constant, wires it into the admin toggle list, and runs typecheck.

oneOf.description: Copies template files into a target directory, resolving workflow-area markers along the way.

templateFiles.description: Map of file id to source path. TBD (Phase 3): how a config-defined workflow's own template sources are stored and resolved — this is not yet a path on the runner's disk.

targetDir.description: Directory (relative to the run's cwd) the copied files land in.

name.description: kebab-case name substituted for `template-file` and its case variants.

oneOf.description: Prompts the agent to edit a file a `copy` step already produced, blocking on TODO markers until resolved.

fileId.description: Id into the accumulated `copiedFiles` map from prior `copy` steps.

prompt.description: Instruction shown to the agent. Defaults to a generic "update this file" prompt.
prompt.example: Wire the new flag into the admin toggle list.

oneOf.description: Prompts the agent (or, in `print` mode, the caller) to do an arbitrary task.

prompt.example: Run the drizzle migration and confirm it applied cleanly.

ignoreError.description: Treat a non-zero exit as success.

errorPrompt.description: Extra text shown to the agent alongside the failure, in `run` mode.

forceInScript.description: Run even in `script` mode if it would otherwise be treated as a skipped validation command (typecheck/test).

oneOf.description: Changes the working directory for subsequent steps.

path.description: Absolute, or relative to the run's original working directory.

oneOf.description: Runs `npm run <script> -w <workspace>`, validating both exist first.
